evals.prompt: /anatoly the trap under a kitchen sink, interactive: you open the tap and see what happens. One standalone HTML file, light theme.
evals.expected_output: Claude reads ANATOMY.md, sizes the job (a Figure or a Hero) and says so before building. The build holds a bodge ledger (ledger().assert() passes) with 5–9 entries for a Figure, a junk structure under the sink readable at 1× (the trap held up by a stick, string or a brick), exactly one hero bodge readable at 1× (for example the trap's main joint held by tape alone), every entry with a kind, where, why and the failure it feeds. The page is an Anatomy-quality isometric figure in a job-ticket card (Job number, title, deadpan hint such as 'open the tap.', status readout with true numbers such as a drip rate). Opening the tap works first, strains, pauses, then the taped joint lets go and the trap falls apart: its pieces drop one after another, land on the cabinet floor, tip over or rock flat, and water runs out into a puddle; the motion is driven by failureClock, shakeAt, fallAt, tipAt and rockAt with no pop, and 'r' or the 'call Anatoly to fix it' button, shown only while it's broken, calls Anatoly, plays the failure back with no jump and adds one more band of tape. Repair material is in the repair colour only. The --honest build, the bodged build (with only B.auditOptions()), each --broken pose and --repairs=max all end 'audit passed', lines.mjs prints 'line ends: 0', and every PNG was looked at.

evals.prompt: I'm making a nostalgia game. Build a 90s cassette deck that Anatoly installed: piano-key buttons for play, rewind and eject, two reels you can see through the cassette window, VU needles. Pressing play should work for a second and then eat the tape. Standalone HTML, light theme, no figure card since it's a game screen.
evals.expected_output: Claude uses Anatoly on top of Anatomy, says it is a Hero and roughly how long it will take, and honours the request to drop the card (the job ticket's words move to the game's own UI or are left out, as asked). The deck is a dense, precise isometric machine with 10–18 ledger bodges (for example a rubber-band belt, a taped cassette door, a shimmed foot, a mismatched knob, a needle mounted upside down), one hero bodge visible at 1×. Play runs the reels (the one with the slipping belt slower, with a true speed in the status), then the tape spills out as a sag or loop and the reels jam; rewind and eject have their own outcome tables from outcomeOf. Reels turn by rebuilding their spokes per frame or turning a texture, not with a screen rotation. Gives are drawable in the page; anything that tips is precomputed or turned on screen about its rim (tipAt, turnAbout). Fix plays back and adds a repair. Reduced motion, keyboard and aria follow Anatomy. All four audits and the line check pass.

evals.prompt: For our 404 page I want a janky, duct-taped espresso machine that sputters and breaks when you pull a shot. React component for Next.js, dark theme.
evals.expected_output: The skill triggers without being named. Claude follows Anatomy's React split (geometry in .ts modules, static art in a server component with the draw.tsx components, one 'use client' live component) and inlines Anatoly's helpers or imports kit/anatoly.mjs in the client component. The machine carries a bodge ledger with a hero bodge, the pull works for a moment, strains, then gives (a gasket taped, a portafilter that drops, steam from the wrong place), driven from failureClock with no per-frame React re-render. Repair colour in both themes via kit/anatoly.css. Audits and checks as in Anatomy plus Anatoly's four builds.

evals.prompt: Make a clean, polished isometric figure explaining how a token bucket rate limiter works, for our docs. Light theme, standalone HTML.
evals.expected_output: The user explicitly asks for a clean figure, so Claude does not break it: it follows ANATOMY.md alone and builds a working, precise figure with no bodges, no ledger, no failure and no job ticket.

evals.prompt: Build an interactive isometric hand-cranked coffee grinder. One HTML file.
evals.expected_output: The request never says broken, but Claude uses Anatoly and doesn't ask whether to break it: it says in one line that this is Anatoly's install and that it falls apart when used, sizes the job and builds on Anatomy's workflow. The grinder sits on a junk structure readable at 1×: log or fence-post legs on bricks or breeze blocks, rope lashings, a crooked stick brace, a plank base, tape on several joints, and a hero bodge on the load path (for example the hopper or the crank held on with tape only, with empty bolt holes where the screws should be). The ledger asserts, with the junk structure as entries. The main control's outcome table falls apart on every use: turning the crank works for a moment, strains and sags, then the hero joint tears and three to five pieces fall one after another with a seeded stagger, spin, land on a rim and come to rest in different poses (tipped over, leaning, rocked flat), all on the base. The 'call Anatoly to fix it' button is hidden at rest and appears once it's broken; it and 'r' play the collapse back with no jump and add a band of tape. The honest build, the bodged build and the landed states all end 'audit passed', line ends are 0 at rest and broken, and the slowed contact sheet of the collapse was looked at.
